title: Semantic Enhanced Text-to-SQL Parsing via Iteratively Learning Schema Linking Graph

problem.claim: Text-to-SQL systems need to generalize to new databases when parsing human utterances into SQL statements.

gap.claim: Exact matching methods fail when question words and schema items have different surface forms, such as under synonym substitution.

contributions.claim: ISESL-SQL iteratively builds a semantically enhanced schema-linking graph between question tokens and database schemas.
The framework extracts a schema-linking graph from pretrained language models through unsupervised probing and optimizes it during training with deep graph learning.
The framework introduces graph regularization as an auxiliary task to improve schema information represented in the schema-linking graph.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three benchmarks reportedly show that ISESL-SQL consistently outperforms the baselines.
The authors report that further investigations show generalizability and robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generalization to new databases is identified as important for Text-to-SQL systems.
Existing approaches use exact matching to identify lexical links between questions and schemas.
Exact matching fails when corresponding question and schema terms differ in surface form.
ISESL-SQL constructs and refines a semantic schema-linking graph using probing, graph learning, and graph regularization.
The authors report consistent baseline improvements across three benchmarks and further evidence of generalizability and robustness.

source_observation.claim: Surface-form matching can fail when semantically corresponding question and schema terms use synonyms.

interpretation.claim: Schema linking should represent semantic relationships beyond exact lexical overlap.

application.claim: Use an iteratively learned semantic graph to connect question tokens with database schemas.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach remains effective for database domains or language phenomena beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three benchmarks, datasets, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not quantify the reported improvements over baselines.
The abstract does not describe the probing procedure, graph-learning architecture, or graph-regularization objective in detail.
